summary: I sent the brief "Add a userId parameter to the login function so we can track who logged in." The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming before doing anything else and said outright "Classification: architectural, not bounded." It asked clarifying questions, then presented the design in two sections and asked me to confirm each. It wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-10-03-login-user-tracking-design.md and asked me to review it. No app code was touched before that. After I said "looks good, go ahead", it moved on to hyperpowers:writing-plans.
reasoning: All five criteria were met, with evidence from the screen, the files on disk and the session log. The agent escalated to architectural explicitly, wrote the spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/, asked for review before writing any code, and only began implementation planning after I approved.

observations.description: The agent pushed back on the brief well. It explained that userId should be returned by login rather than passed in, because a client-supplied ID can be spoofed. It kept the login(username, password) signature and proposed a shared session.js module.

The Codex spec review did not complete. The agent said both passes "exited cleanly but returned an empty {} with no verdict" and that the companion reports version "0.0.0-stub". This is the expected result of the seeded stub. The agent said clearly that the spec has had no Codex review and recorded the skipped review for a later re-run (event 20261003T213155Z-43729-19433), so the gap was not hidden from the user.
The spec was left uncommitted ("not committed"). Criterion 4 mentions a "committed spec file", so graders should know the file is on disk but untracked (git status shows "?? docs/").

On first launch Claude Code showed several onboarding prompts: theme, security notes, folder trust, and "Newer Opus model available" (it said "Currently pinned: Opus 5" even though --model claude-opus-5-5 was passed). The folder trust prompt has "No, exit" selected by default. I declined the model update and the banner then showed Opus 5.5.
The spec header reads "Status: Approved design, pending spec review" even though I had not yet approved the spec document itself.

criteria.evidence: Screen: "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". The jq listing of tool_use entries in the session JSONL has {"name":"Skill","i":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"} as its first entry. The only tools called before it are read-only Bash/grep.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before asking for approval
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Classification: architectural, not bounded. ... I'll take the heavier path: questions, then a design, then your approval before any code." Later: "That confirms it's architectural." `ls docs/hyperpowers/specs` → 2026-10-03-login-user-tracking-design.md (header: "# Login User Tracking — Design ... Status: Approved design, pending spec review").

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-10-03-login-user-tracking-design.md (not committed)... Please review the spec and tell me if you want any changes before I write the implementation plan." At that point `git status --short` showed only "?? docs/" and `git diff --stat` was empty, so app.js and index.html were untouched. The log's only Write call before my approval was the spec file.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: The agent explicitly rejected bounded ("architectural, not bounded") and wrote a spec file to disk. I never saw an in-chat-only short design.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / probe plan
criteria.evidence: The agent never mentioned a spike, a probe or throwaway work. The tool sequence in the session log is brainstorming → AskUserQuestion x3 → Write spec → Codex review attempt → writing-plans.
